correctness.rationale: A unitary Zak transform diagonalizes the union of two integer-frequency critical lattices, with multiplier |Zg_w(x,omega)|^2+|Zg_w(x,omega-delta)|^2. The Fourier transform pi/w exp(-2pi w|xi|) gives a closed rational Zak fiber. Its modulus-square derivative with respect to cos(2pi x) is strictly positive because p,q are nonnegative and the positive denominator is cubed; hence minima at x=1/2, maxima at x=0. Strict convexity of sinh^2 and cosh^2 along the two frequency intervals gives exactly the asserted essential extrema and their attaining fibers. The d=min(delta,1-delta) dependence makes 1/2 the unique optimizer. Taylor sinh(pi w delta)=pi w delta+O(delta^3) gives the quadratic coefficient.
risk: Claim assumes precisely unit translation and two unit-frequency cosets; does not extend to arbitrary irregular sets.
Finite numerical tests do not prove the continuous extrema or all w and delta.

originality.rationale: Belov and Semenov (October 21, 2026) give a sharp existence criterion for irregular/semi-regular Poisson-kernel Gabor systems, including the two-coset configuration as a qualitative frame case. That prior work covers existence, not exact optimal lower/upper constants, global optimal staggering or delta^2 coalescence coefficient. The balanced delta=1/2 case also belongs to known regular half-frequency lattice formulas. Full off-balance quantitative profile survives this statement-level comparison.
